sections.content: How many people are "call and contact centre occupations"?

48,165 people

were counted on the census as "call and contact centre occupations" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Call and contact centre occupations receive and respond to telephone calls from potential clients and existing customers regarding the products and services offered by an organisation.

People who had this job were generally younger

The occupation of "call and contact centre occupations" had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "call and contact centre occupations", 22.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "call and contact centre occupations" was 65 years or older.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "call and contact centre occupations" included:

  • bar and catering supervisors
  • early education and childcare assistants
  • telephone salespersons

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "call and contact centre occupations" there were more women than men (63.5% compared with 36.5%).

This means "call and contact centre occupations" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "customer service occupations".

Men made up 36.5% and women made up 63.5% of "call and contact centre occupations"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "call and contact centre occupations" included:

  • pharmacists
  • charitable organisation managers and directors
  • project support officers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "call and contact centre occupations" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "call and contact centre occupations" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "call and contact centre occupations", 15.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (70.6% compared with 29.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98.8%) than self-employed (1.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Sheffield, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
